subject: chemistry
question_text: Calculate the ratio of kinetic energies of 3 g of hydrogen and 4 g of oxygen at a given temperature.

verification.note: Chapter 4 (States of Matter) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.62-66), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The book prints NO Long Answer section for this chapter, so no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Arithmetic checked: 1.5 mol : 0.125 mol = 12 : 1, matching the book.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The principle and the moles
lines: KE = (3/2) nRT. At the same temperature the
kinetic energies are in the ratio of the moles.
steps.why: R and T are common to both gases, so they cancel in the ratio and only the mole numbers remain. The whole question reduces to two gram-to-mole conversions.
common_mistakes: Taking the ratio of the masses 3 : 4. Kinetic energy follows moles, not grams.
Using M(H₂) = 1. Hydrogen gas is diatomic, M = 2 g mol⁻¹.
steps.memory_tip: Same T means R and T cancel: the KE ratio IS the mole ratio.
steps.margin_note: Stating that the ratio of energies equals the ratio of moles is the marked idea.

steps.label: The ratio
steps.why: Dividing both sides by 0.125 gives 12 on the left and 1 on the right. A ratio is reported in the smallest whole numbers.
common_mistakes: Leaving the ratio as 1.5 : 0.125 instead of 12 : 1.
Writing 1 : 12 — hydrogen has more moles, so its energy is the larger side.
steps.memory_tip: Three grams of the lightest gas is a lot of moles; four grams of oxygen is very few. The light gas side is far larger: 12 to 1.
steps.margin_note: A ratio has no unit; 12 : 1 in whole numbers is the expected form.

insider_note: No temperature value is given on purpose — spotting that T cancels and the answer is a pure mole ratio is what earns the marks.
